Networkingk8s 1.35

Wiring a Pod via CNI

Who actually runs the CNI plugins, and in what order? The Kubelet asks the CRI runtime for a Pod sandbox, then the runtime, not the Kubelet, reads the plugin list from /etc/cni/net.d and runs each as an executable, handing every one after the first the previous result as prevResult. The bridge plugin delegates addressing to its own host-local IPAM plugin, the last plugin prints one result of interfaces, addresses, routes and DNS, and DEL runs the list in reverse.

▶ Play the animation 6 steps, animated, best on a wide screen

How it works, step by step

  1. The Kubelet asks the CRI runtime, here containerd, for a Pod sandbox, and the runtime starts the pause container that owns the network namespace. For now that namespace holds loopback only and no Pod IP. The plugin chain that follows runs inside that one RunPodSandbox call.

    Play from this step

  2. The runtime, not the Kubelet, reads the plugin list from /etc/cni/net.d and runs the first plugin as a plain executable. CNI_COMMAND=ADD, the sandbox namespace path and CNI_IFNAME=eth0 arrive on its environment, and the network config arrives on stdin.

    Play from this step

  3. The bridge plugin does not hand out addresses itself. Its config names an IPAM plugin, host-local, which it runs as a delegate of its own, and host-local picks 10.244.1.5 out of the range for this Node and returns it to the caller.

    Play from this step

  4. The runtime then runs the next plugin in the list. It passes the previous result in as prevResult, so portmap adds to what bridge already produced instead of starting over. That ordered list is what the word chain means here.

    Play from this step

  5. The last plugin prints one result on stdout: the interfaces the chain made, the addresses on them, the routes and the DNS. The one the chain made inside the sandbox namespace comes up as eth0 carrying 10.244.1.5, and the operation finishes as ADD ok.

    Play from this step

  6. Only now does the Kubelet start the app containers, and they join the namespace that is already wired, so all of them answer on that one Pod IP. On delete the runtime runs the same list with CNI_COMMAND=DEL, in reverse order, and each plugin releases what it made.

    Play from this step
